text: he everybody this is your regular reminder that there is no God of the Bible and I don't mean that in some kind of EDG Lord all gods are fairy tales way
what I mean by it is that the Bible presents numerous different and often contradictory conceptualizations of God
there are many different gods of the Bible and when we talk about the God of the Bible what we're doing is taking
this Corpus of texts which was compartmentalized centuries after all the texts within it were written by the
way and we're identifying those conceptualizations of God that are going to be most meaningful and useful to us
in given sets of circumstances and we're kind of giving them priority and marginalizing or ignoring the conceptualizations that we don't like
and so in one set of circumstances we may arrange those conceptualizations so that the god of the Bible appears a
certain way and in another set of circumstances we may rearrange those conceptualizations so that the god of
the Bible appears a different way and so there is no single god of the Bible there are numerous different gods of the
Bible and therein lies one of the central reasons that the god of the Bible has dominated for as long as they
have it's precisely because the numerous different conceptualizations allow those Divine profiles to be customized to the
given set of circumstances and to the rhetorical needs and so the god of the Bible can be whatever their people need them
